binders: rate : NNReal, an arbitrary nonnegative real rate
k : Nat, an arbitrary natural-number index
conclusions: The Poisson measure with rate rate assigns the singleton set {k} the extended-nonnegative-real value ENNReal.ofReal(exp(-rate) * rate^k / k!).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 rate unfolds through LocalDef002 rate to ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure rate.
The singleton {k} is the set containing exactly the natural number k.
The right-hand expression is computed in Real as exp(-(rate : Real)) * (rate : Real)^k / (k! : Real), then mapped to ENNReal by ENNReal.ofReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative real rate and every natural number k, the Poisson measure with that rate assigns mass exp(-rate) times rate to the kth power divided by k factorial to the singleton containing k.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The rate is restricted by its type to nonnegative real values; no separate nonnegativity hypothesis appears.
The index k ranges over all natural numbers, including zero.
There are no hypotheses, so the proposition is not vacuously true through an inconsistent or unsatisfiable premise.

The formula is embedded with ENNReal.ofReal, which would truncate a negative real input to zero; here the displayed quotient is nonnegative because the rate is nonnegative, the exponential is positive, the natural power is nonnegative, and k! is positive.
At rate = 0 and k = 0, the formula depends on the natural-power convention 0^0 = 1 and gives exp(0) / 0! = 1.
At rate = 0 and positive k, the formula gives zero.
ambiguities: The target does not state normalization or any other characterization of the measure; it asserts only the singleton-value formula.
The presence of ENNReal.ofReal syntactically permits truncation, although the quantified domain makes the displayed real expression nonnegative.
